FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards after the draft finalized by the Spices and 
Condiments Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council. 

Tamarind powder {Tamarindus indica L) is an important condiment used daily as a sour ingredient in the Indian 
cookery. India produces about 2.5 lakh tonnes of tamarind pulp per annum, bulk of it coming from the states of 
Madhya Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Orissa, and to a limited extent from Bihar, Maharashtra and 
Kamataka. For better compactness and for greater convenience in use and handling a method has now been 
standardized for the production of dehydrated free flowing tamarind powder. 

Tamarind pulp, as obtained from the trade is manually cleaned deseeded and fibre removed. The pulp is processed 
under standardized conditions of temperature and humidity to obtain an acceptable product in a powder fonn 
possessing good reconstitutional characteristics. 

This standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1 954 and Rules 
framed thereunder, wherever applicable. 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observedorcalculated,expressingtheresultofatestoranalysis,shallberoundedoff inaccordauce with IS 2 : 1960 
'Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)\ The number of significant places retained in the rounded off 
value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 



IS 13895 : 19M 



Indian Standard 

SPICES AND CONDIMENTS — TAMARIND 
POWDER — SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 



1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements for 
tamarind powder. 

2 REFERENCES 

2*1 The following Indian Standards are necessary 
adjuncts to this standard: 

IS No. rule 

1797 : 1985 Methods of test for spices and 

condiments {second revision) 

2491 : 1972 Code for hygienic conditions for 

food processing units {first revision) 

5955 : 1993 Spices and condiments — Tamarind 

concentrate — Specification 

7807 : 1975 Method of test for asafoetida 

13145 : 1993 Spice and condiments — Methods of 
sampling {first revision) 

3 REQUIREMENTS 

3.1 Description 

The tamarind powder shall be prepared from cleaned, 
deseeded, defibrinated tamarind pulp under stand- 
ardized conditions of temperature and humidity. 

3.2 Freedom from Fungal Growth and Insect 
Infestation, etc 

The tamarind powder shall be free from fungal growth 
and insect infestation when examined by naked eye 
(corrected for abnormal vision). 

3.3 The tamarind powder shall also comply with the 
requirements given in Table 1. 

3.4 Tamarind powder shall be manufactured and pack- 
ed under hygienic conditions {see IS 2491 : 1972). 



4 PACKING AND MARKING 

4.1 Packing 

The tamarind powder shall be packed only in sound, 
clean, and dry containers made of tin, glass or paper 
carton lined with a polyethylene liner of 300 gauge; or 
laminated aluminium foil packs; or cellophane bags. If 
a polyethylene liner is used in tin-plate containers, it 
may be 150 gauge. The container shall be free from any 
fungal or insect- infestation and shall be free from any 
undesirable smell. 

4.1.1 Small containers may be packed in wooden or 
cardboard cases. 

4.2 Marldng 

The following particulars shall be marked or labelled 
on each container: 

a) Name of the material and the trade-mark or brand 
name, if any; 

b) Name and address of the manufacturer; 

c) Batch or code number; 

d) Net mass; and 

e) Date of packing. 

4.2.1 If the containers are packed in cases, each case 
shall also be marked with the particulars (a) to (e) in 4.2. 

5 SAMPLING AND TESTS 



Representative sample of the material shall be drawn as 
prescribed in IS 13145 : 1993. The sample of tamarind 
powder shall be tested for ascertaining conformity of 
the material to the requirements of this specification by 
the methods of test given in IS 1797 : 1985 and 
IS 7807 : 1975.
